Sociologist Khagendra Bista, representing the High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilisation, defended the government’s transport arrangements. “The Ministry of Education coordinated transportation for students, while the Ministry of Labour managed transit for working adults,” said Bista. “We offered to enrol the children in schools near the new holding centres, but the parents insisted on keeping them in their original schools. We arranged the buses to respect their wishes.”

Bista acknowledged the two-week gap in education for children at Ichangunarayan, stating that local officials have now coordinated with nearby community schools to ensure all displaced children resume their studies.

Educationalists, however, argue that lengthy commutes inflict unnecessary hardship on young learners. Professor Bidya Nath Koirala said that spending three to four hours daily in traffic severely impacts children’s health and learning capacity.

“Subjecting young children to two two-hour commutes daily in heavy traffic is an immense burden,” said Koirala. “The municipal authorities and school administrators must establish dialogue immediately to integrate these displaced children into schools located in the immediate vicinity of the holding centres.”

articles.title: सुर्खेतमा ग्यास अभाव छैन : आयल निगम
articles.summary:
नेपाल आयल निगम सुर्खेतले वीरेन्द्रनगरमा एलपी ग्यासको अभाव नभएको स्पष्ट गरेको छ।

निगमका अनुसार भारतबाट आवश्यक परिमाणमा एलपी ग्यास नियमित रुपमा आयात भइरहेको छ।

पछिल्लो समय अभाव हुन सक्ने मनोवैज्ञानिक त्रासका कारण आवश्यकताभन्दा बढी ग्यास सञ्चय गर्ने प्रवृत्ति बढेकाले बजारमा वितरणमा केही प्रभाव देखिएको नेपाल आयल निगम सुर्खेतका प्रमुख दिपक कुमार घिमिरेले जानकारी दिए।

उपभोक्ताको सहजताका लागि ‘एक व्यक्ति, एक सिलिन्डर’ को व्यवस्था लागू गरी अधिकृत बिक्रेतामार्फत विभिन्न कम्पनीका दुई हजार ९२२ वटा एलपी ग्यास १४ दशमलव २ केजीको प्रति सिलिन्डर रु दुई हजार ६० मा बिक्री–वितरण गरिने प्रमुख घिमिरेले बताए।

त्यस्तै, नेपाल ग्यासका ३२० वटा सिलिन्डर वीरेन्द्रनगर औद्योगिक क्षेत्रमा रहेको न्यू जानकी ट्रेड एण्ड सप्लायर्समार्फत वितरण गरिने निगमले जनाएको छ।

नेपाल आयल निगमले उपभोक्तालाई अधिकृत बिक्रेताबाट मात्र ग्यास खरिद गर्न, अनावश्यक रुपमा ग्यास सञ्चय नगर्न तथा तोकिएको मूल्यभन्दा बढी रकम असुल गरेको, मौज्दात हुँदाहुँदै ग्यास बिक्री नगरेको वा अनधिकृत रुपमा सञ्चय गरेको जानकारी भएमा तत्काल सम्बन्धित निकायमा जानकारी गराउन अनुरोध गरेको छ।

articles.title: सोनमले अनशन तोडेपछि सरकार र सीजेपीबिच उच्चस्तरीय वार्ता हुँदै
articles.summary:
दिल्लीमा जारी राजनीतिक गतिरोध अन्त्य गर्न सरकार र ककरोच जनता पार्टी (सीजेपी) बिच आज नेपाली समय अनुसार दिउँसो १२:४५ बजे (स्थानीय समय १२:३० बजे) दोस्रो चरणको वार्ता हुने भएको छ।

यसअघि केन्द्रीय स्वास्थ्यमन्त्री जेपी नड्डाको निवासमा भएको पहिलो चरणको वार्ता निष्कर्षमा पुग्न सकेको थिएन। त्यसयता सरकार र सीजेपीबिचको सम्बन्ध खराब बन्दै गएको थियो। सरकारले यसअघि सीजेपीलाई वार्ताका लागि चार पटक आमन्त्रण गरे पनि उनीहरू उपस्थित भएनन्। सीजेपी केन्द्रीय मन्त्री जेपी नड्डाको निवासमा नभई तटस्थ स्थानमा मात्र वार्ता हुनुपर्ने अडान राख्दै आएको थियो। सोही अडानस्वरूप आजको वार्ता तटस्थ स्थल मानिएको कन्स्टिट्यूशन क्लबमा हुन लागेको हो।

सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता सोनम वाङ्चुकले २६ औं दिनमा आफ्नो आमरण अनशन तोडेपछि यो वार्ता हुन लागेको हो। केन्द्रीय मन्त्रीहरू जेपी नड्डा र जितेन्द्र सिंहले मेदान्त अस्पताल पुगेर उनलाई जुस खुवाएपछि उनले अनशन अन्त्य गरेका हुन्। वाङ्चुकले अनशन तोडेसँगै सरकारले उनका केही प्रमुख मागहरूप्रति सकारात्मक प्रतिक्रिया दिएको छ।

मन्त्री नड्डाले वाङचुकसमक्ष सरकारका निर्णयहरू पढेर सुनाएका थिए। सरकारले जन्तरमन्तरमा शान्तिपूर्ण प्रदर्शन गर्नेहरू र जुलाई २० मा ‘संसद् चलो’ मार्चमा सहभागी भएका विद्यार्थीहरूविरुद्ध कुनै पनि मुद्दा दर्ता नगर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ।

यसका साथै, हालैका घटनाहरूमा ज्यान गुमाएका विद्यार्थीका परिवारलाई उचित क्षतिपूर्ति दिने र पेपर चुहावट तथा परीक्षा प्रणालीमा जवाफदेहिता सुनिश्चित गर्न संसदमा गम्भीर बहस चलाउने कुरामा सरकार सकारात्मक देखिएको छ।

वार्ताको पूर्वसन्ध्यामा सीजेपीले सरकारमाथि दबाब बढाउँदै देशव्यापी विरोध प्रदर्शनको घोषणा गरेको छ। सीजेपीका संस्थापक अभिजीत दिपके र प्रवक्ता आशुतोष राँकाले केन्द्रीय शिक्षा मन्त्री धर्मेन्द्र प्रधानले राजीनामा नदिएसम्म जन्तरमन्तरमा विरोध प्रदर्शन जारी रहने प्रस्ट पारेका छन्।

प्रवक्ता राँकाले भने, ‘सरकार हाम्रो अत्यधिक दबाबमा छ, जसका कारण प्रधानमन्त्रीले राति अबेर भिडियो जारी गर्नुपर्‍यो। मन्त्रिपरिषद्का निर्णयहरू र प्रधानमन्त्रीको भिडियोले मात्र हामी पछि हट्ने छैनौँ। शिक्षामन्त्रीको राजीनामा नभएसम्म हाम्रो संघर्ष रोकिनेछैन।’

प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले बिहीबार राति जारी गरेको भिडियो सन्देशमा पेपर चुहावटसम्बन्धी कडा कानुन ल्याइने र दोषीहरूलाई सजाय दिन फास्ट-ट्र्याक अदालतहरू स्थापना गरिने बताएका थिए। आज मोदीको अध्यक्षतामा बस्ने केन्द्रीय मन्त्रिपरिषद्को बैठक दिउँसो १:१५ बजे संसद् भवन, नयाँ दिल्लीमा बस्दैछ।

साथै, अनशन तोडेका वाङ्चुकको स्वास्थ्य लाभको कामना गर्दै उनले चिकित्सकको सल्लाह पालना गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

यसैबिच, विपक्षी दलका शीर्ष नेताहरूले सरकारको कार्यशैलीप्रति असन्तुष्टि व्यक्त गरेका छन्। कांग्रेस नेता मल्लिकार्जुन खड्गेले संसद्को अधिवेशन चलिरहेको अवस्थामा प्रधानमन्त्रीले बाहिर एकतर्फी भिडियो जारी गर्नुको सट्टा संसद् भवनभित्रै जवाफ दिनुपर्ने बताए।

कांग्रेसकी वरिष्ठ नेतृ सोनिया गान्धीले मोदी सरकारले विद्यार्थीहरूको जायज आवाजलाई कायरता र क्रूरतापूर्वक दबाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाइन्।

लोकसभामा प्रतिपक्षी दलका नेता राहुल गान्धीले शिक्षामन्त्रीको राजीनामा, लाठीचार्ज गर्नेहरूमाथि कारबाही र पीडित विद्यार्थीहरूसँग माफी माग्नुपर्ने तीनबुधे माग राख्दै प्रधानमन्त्रीको भिडियोले आन्दोलन नरोकिने स्पष्ट पारेका छन्।

विरोध प्रदर्शनलाई मध्यनजर गर्दै दिल्लीमा सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारिएको छ। दिल्ली मेट्रो रेल कर्पोरेसनले राजीव चौक, लोक कल्याण मार्ग, मन्डी हाउस, केन्द्रीय सचिवालयलगायत १७ वटा प्रमुख मेट्रो स्टेसनहरू अर्को सूचना नभएसम्मका लागि बन्द गरेको छ।

यद्यपि, मुख्य इन्टरचेन्ज स्टेसनहरूमा भने सीमित रूपमा आवागमन खुला राखिएको छ। जन्तरमन्तरमा लगाइएको इन्टरनेटको बन्देजविरुद्ध दायर रिटमा दिल्ली उच्च अदालतमा आज सुनुवाइ हुँदैछ।

यसअघि शिक्षा मन्त्रालयमा ठूलो प्रशासनिक फेरबदल गर्दै सरकारले उच्च शिक्षा विभाग र स्कुल शिक्षा तथा साक्षरता विभागका सचिवहरूलाई फेरिसकेको छ।

articles.title: बागमतीका १३ वटै जिल्लाका उद्योग प्रशासन डिजिटल प्रणालीमा
articles.summary:
बागमती प्रदेश सरकारले बागमती प्रदेशका १३ वटै जिल्लाको उद्योग प्रशासन सेवा डिजिटल प्रणाली (अनलाइन सेवा) मा सञ्चालन गर्ने तयारी गरेको छ।

उद्योग तथा वाणिज्य कार्यालय मकवानपुरबाट उद्योग प्रशासनमा (उद्योग दर्ता, नवीकरण, नामसारी लगायतका सेवा) अनलाइन प्रणालीमार्फत सेवा सुरु गरेको मन्त्रालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३/०८४ मा प्रदेशका १३ वटै जिल्लाहरूमा उद्योग प्रशासन सेवा अनलाइन मार्फत सञ्चालन गर्ने तयारी गरेको मन्त्रालयका प्रवक्ता कुमार तामाङले जानकारी दिए।

प्रदेश अन्तर्गत चितवन, काभ्रेपलाञ्चोक, रामेछाप र सिन्धुलीका उद्योग तथा वाणिज्य कार्यालयहरूलाई नमूना कार्यालय घोषणा गरिसकेको मन्त्रालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३/८४ मा १३ वटै कार्यालयलाई नमूना कार्यालय बनाउने लक्ष्य सहित बजेट विनियोजन गरिएको जनाएको छ।

मन्त्रालयले नमूना कार्यालय व्यवस्थापन मापदण्ड समेत तयार गरिसकेको छ। प्रदेशमा आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ को असार मसान्तसम्म मन्त्रालय मातहत करिब चार हजार ९५६ उद्योग र दुई हजार ५५० वाणिज्य फर्म दर्ता भएका छन्।

बजारमा कालोबजारी तथा कृतिम अभाव नियन्त्रणका लागि नियमित र आकस्मिक बजार अनुगमनलाई निरन्तरता दिइएको मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: In Sudurpaschim, tourists are coming. Infrastructure isn’t
articles.summary:
On a fine morning last month, a jeep carrying domestic tourists from Bajhang, Dhangadhi and Dadeldhura climbed a dirt road towards Jadalek in Saipal Rural Municipality, Bajhang. Lured by breathtaking photographs and videos shared on social media, the group had travelled hundreds of kilometres to visit the southern base camp of Mount Saipal (7031 metres), the western base camp at Raidughi and the secluded Maza valley, surrounded by towering snow-covered peaks.

Their trek began from Dhalaun, passing Kakarkot before reaching the southern and western base camps. Things were normal until then and the trekkers were excited. But once they left Raidughi for Maza valley, around four hours away, their excitement gave way to fear. The narrow mountain trail soon disappeared beneath thick shrubs, leaving only a precarious footpath clinging to steep cliffs.

“There was barely enough space to place one foot,” said trekker Bir Bahadur Dhami. “We held onto bushes as we moved forward, but eventually there was nowhere safe to step.”

Looking down, Dhami went on, “all we could see was a sheer drop”. Some of the trekkers felt dizzy and the team decided to abandon the trip. “We decided risking our lives was not worth it,” Dhami said.

Dhami said even simple trail markers would have helped visitors navigate safely. Instead, the group abandoned the journey despite coming so close to their destination.

Their experience reflects a wider problem across Sudurpaschim. The province is home to some of Nepal’s most spectacular landscapes that are drawing increasing numbers of visitors but remain constrained by poor tourism infrastructure. Social media has introduced destinations such as Api and Saipal mountains, Khaptad, Badimalika and the Api-Nampa Conservation Area to millions of viewers, yet tourists continue to complain about inadequate trails, limited accommodation, unreliable communications and the absence of basic visitor facilities.

The mismatch between growing demand and weak infrastructure has prevented the region from realising its enormous tourism potential, despite possessing world-class natural attractions.

Until only a few years ago, Khaptad, Saipal and Api attracted mostly experienced trekkers, researchers and mountaineers. Today, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok have transformed them into sought-after destinations for domestic travellers.

Interest in Api surged after Prime Minister Balendra Shah posted a short Facebook video of people playing cricket at Api Base Camp. Earlier, while addressing an election rally in Sudurpaschim, Shah had described Badimalika and Ramaroshan as ‘the father of Switzerland’, a remark that quickly went viral and sparked curiosity about the mountain destination.

Colourful images of Khaptad’s rolling grasslands, the vast alpine meadows of Badimalika and the dramatic peaks of Api and Saipal continue to circulate widely online, encouraging more Nepalis to visit every year. Official figures also indicate rising visitor numbers, although local authorities say government records significantly underestimate arrivals.

According to the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation under the Ministry of Forests and Environment, 29 foreign tourists visited the Api-Nampa Conservation Area during the fiscal year 2024-25. However, Api Himal Rural Municipality says more than 5,000 tourists reach Api Base Camp annually.

“The department’s records are based on reports prepared from the district headquarters and differ greatly from the actual number of visitors,” said Bhagat Singh Bohara, chairman of Api Himal Rural Municipality. “Our municipal records show that more than 5,000 tourists, including around 150 foreigners, have visited Api every year over the past three years.”

Among Sudurpaschim’s major trekking destinations, the Api Base Camp trail is generally considered to have the region’s best infrastructure. The trekking route features a relatively safe footpath leading to the base camp, along with four guest houses, four tea shops and homestays operating in five villages along the trail.

Even there, however, infrastructure has failed to keep pace with demand.

“During the Nepali New Year and the Dashain and Tihar holidays, we struggle to accommodate visitors,” said Bohara. “Our facilities can host around 60 people a day, but on one occasion about 250 tourists arrived together. We had to arrange tents and even use shelters built for yarsagumba collectors. We managed somehow, but the existing infrastructure is still inadequate.”

According to Bohara, additional guest houses with larger capacities, designated camping sites, upgraded trekking trails and proper waste-management systems are urgently needed.

Khaptad National Park has experienced a similar surge in popularity. Department figures show that annual visitor numbers, which ranged from just 19 to 46 between the fiscal years 2012-13 and 2017-18, have increased to around 3,000 every year since 2018-19.

Yet the infrastructure has not expanded accordingly in the area. During peak seasons, visitors often struggle to find accommodation and spend freezing nights without adequate shelter. Others lose their way because of insufficient trail signs, while expensive tourism infrastructure funded by the state remains unused.

One striking example is a prefabricated accommodation complex near the park headquarters and another at Bichpani built for travellers entering through Doti. The facilities, designed to accommodate 150 visitors and equipped with technology to keep rooms warm even in freezing conditions, were funded by the Nepal Tourism Board under the 2018-19 fiscal budget.

Construction began in 2019 and the buildings were completed several years ago. Despite this, the accommodation has yet to open for visitors. Trekkers continue sleeping in the cold while posing for photographs outside the locked buildings the following morning.

“We have repeatedly requested everyone, from the chief conservation officer to the department, to bring these buildings into operation,” said Khem Joshi, executive director of the Khaptad Area Tourism Development and Management Committee. “Officials keep saying operational guidelines are being prepared. Meanwhile, the buildings have already started leaking before welcoming a single guest.”

Similar concerns are being raised in Saipal, where annual visitor numbers have increased sharply since the Covid-19 pandemic.

According to Saipal Rural Municipality, an area that received only around 100 to 150 visitors annually before the pandemic now welcomes 300 to 400 tourists each month during the trekking season. Yet flood- and landslide-damaged trails remain unrepaired in several sections, forcing trekkers onto risky paths. In some places, the absence of permanent bridges means visitors must still cross rivers on makeshift log crossings.

Accommodation is available only as far as Dotale, around half a day below Saipal Base Camp. Those wishing to spend the night near the base camp must carry their own tents and supplies.

“We need better trails, bridges and tea houses in several locations,” said Manbir Bohara, chairman of Saipal Rural Municipality. “The rural municipality is working with the Sustainable Tourism Project under the Nepal Tourism Board to improve facilities, including accommodation above Dotale.”

Reaching these mountain destinations remains demanding. Travelling from Kathmandu to Khaptad usually requires around three days, whether entering through Bajhang, Bajura, Doti or Achham. Visitors heading for Saipal travel by road from Dhangadhi through Bajhang district headquarters to Dhalaun before beginning a trek of about one and a half days. Travellers to Api Base Camp first endure a long drive from Dhangadhi to Darchula before trekking for roughly three days from Makarigad.

Tourism campaigner Bharat Bikram Shah said increasing visitor numbers require systematic investment in trekking infrastructure across the region. “Every major route now needs proper trails, information boards, rest areas, rescue points and visitor information centres,” said Shah. “Some sections are unsafe without local guides. We also need trained trekking guides, porters, updated trekking maps for foreign visitors, digital navigation, weather information and emergency communication systems.”

Mobile phone coverage remains another serious challenge. Much of the Saipal and Api trekking routes lies beyond network coverage, complicating rescue efforts during emergencies.

“In many parts of Saipal and Api, mobile networks simply do not work,” said Amar Bahadur Shahi, president of the Korea Tours and Trekking Operators Association Nepal and a tourism entrepreneur. “When someone falls ill or an accident occurs, informing rescuers becomes extremely difficult. Expanding communication networks and maintaining emergency rescue systems are essential if tourism is to grow in remote mountain regions.”

Shahi said inadequate infrastructure also discourages international visitors.

“We may persuade tourists to visit once,” he said. “But if we cannot provide the facilities they expect, they will not return and may even discourage others from coming. Attracting foreign trekkers requires infrastructure that matches international standards.”

Shahi argued that Khaptad, Saipal and Api are valuable not only as trekking destinations but also as centres of biodiversity, Himalayan culture, religious heritage and distinctive mountain lifestyles. If infrastructure expansion, visitor services and conservation progress together, he said, the present surge in interest could become the foundation for sustainable tourism.

Badimalika: Pristine destination devoid of basic infrastructure

Sushma Bhatta, 55, of Dhangadhi has dreamed of visiting Badimalika for years. Yet stories about difficult trails and inadequate accommodation have repeatedly discouraged her from making the journey.

Badimalika, renowned for its religious significance, sweeping alpine meadows and exceptional biodiversity, is among Sudurpaschim’s most celebrated destinations. Nevertheless, visitors continue to face hardships because of poor trekking routes, limited accommodation, shortages of drinking water, inadequate sanitation facilities, weak communication services and a lack of other basic infrastructure.

The destination has received increasing national attention in recent years. The federal government has since included the Shuklaphanta-Khaptad-Badimalika tourism corridor and the Khaptad-Badimalika-Ramaroshan-Budhinanda-Rara-Swargadwari high-altitude eco-trail in its budget for the current fiscal year of 2026-27. The government’s 100-point governance reform agenda also mentions preparing an implementable plan for the Badimalika trekking route. Yet visible progress remains limited.

A provincial task force recently estimated that around Rs1.79 billion would be required to build safe trails, accommodation, drinking water facilities and other essential infrastructure. However, no dedicated allocation was included in Sudurpaschim Province’s budget for the current fiscal year.

Every year, special worship is held at Badimalika Temple on the eve of Janai Purnima. Pilgrims arrive not only from across Nepal but also from Uttarakhand, Kumaon and Garhwal in India, believing their wishes will be fulfilled after offering prayers.

Local officials say the greatest obstacle remains the absence of basic facilities.

“If we truly want tourism to flourish, we must first build fundamental infrastructure,” said Dambar Mahat, ward chair of Badimalika Municipality-2.

Ramsroshan gains popularity, but infrastructure remains unchanged

Ramaroshan in Achham has likewise become increasingly popular because of its pristine lakes, expansive grasslands and rich biodiversity. Yet poor roads, weak communication services and inadequate accommodation continue to make travel difficult, particularly during the monsoon.

Known as the land of ‘12 lakes and 18 meadows’, Ramaroshan stretches from about 2,000 metres to nearly 4,000 metres above sea level. Its largest meadow, Kinemine, covers around 52 bighas, while the Kailash stream winds through the valley.

“Each lake has its own unique character,” said Purna Bahadur BK, executive officer of the Ramaroshan Tourism Development and Management Committee. “During spring, twelve species of rhododendron bloom here. The forests echo with the calls of Himalayan pheasants, while musk deer, Himalayan serow and goral also inhabit the area.”

Local officials say domestic tourist numbers have increased noticeably since Balendra Shah highlighted Ramaroshan during his election campaign. Yet the rough road from Mujabagar remains the greatest barrier.

“Many tourists turn back because of the road,” said local entrepreneur Shamsher Bahadur Bohara. “During the monsoon, rivers and landslides wash away sections of the route. Everyone asks the same question: why is the road still so poor?”

articles.title: सरकारले आवश्यकताअनुसार उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणलाई निरन्तरता दिन्छ : परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालय
articles.summary:
सरकारले सबै मित्रराष्ट्रहरूसँगको सम्बन्धलाई प्रगाढ तुल्याउँदै आवश्यकताअनुसार उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणलाई पनि निरन्तरता दिने जनाएको छ।

परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयमा शुक्रबार आयोजित नियमित पत्रकार सम्मेलनमा सहसचिव एवं प्रवक्ता लोकबहादुर पौडेल क्षेत्रीले प्रचलित कूटनीतिक अभ्यास बमोजिम सरकारले उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणको तयारी गरिरहेको जानकारी दिए।

राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी(रास्वपा)का अनुरोधका आधारमा सभापति रवि लामिछानेको चीन भ्रमणको सहजीकरण गर्न परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालय तयार रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै प्रवक्ता क्षेत्रीले कूटनीतिक आधारमा सबै भ्रमणहरू सम्पन्न हुने बताए।

‘राजनीतिक दलहरूबीच हुने भ्रमण वा आदानप्रदान सम्बन्धित दलहरूको विषय हो। त्यस्तो भ्रमणका लागि परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयको समन्वय वा कूटनीतिक सहजीकरण आवश्यक पर्ने अवस्था आएमा सम्बन्धित राजनीतिक दलको अनुरोधका आधारमा मन्त्रालयले आवश्यक सहजीकरण गर्नेछ’, उनले भने।

एक प्रश्नको जवाफमा उनले प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहका प्रमुख सल्लाहकार कुमार वेनको भारत भ्रमणबारे मन्त्रालय अनभिज्ञ रहेको बताए।

उनले सांस्कृतिक कूटनीति हरेक देशको कूटनीतिक अभ्यासको महत्त्वपूर्ण पक्ष भएको उल्लेख गर्दै यसलाई अझ प्रभावकारी र सुदृढ बनाउने नीति सरकारले लिएको जानकारी समेत दिए।

articles.title: बाग्मती किनारबाट हटाइएका बस्ती क्षेत्रमा खुला पार्क निर्माण गरिने
articles.summary:
बाग्मती नदी किनारबाट हटाइएका अव्यवस्थित बसोबास भएका क्षेत्रलाई खुला सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रका रूपमा विकास गरिने भएको छ।

ती क्षेत्रमा हरित क्षेत्र, खेलमैदान, पदमार्ग (वाकिङ ट्रेल) तथा नदी पुनर्जीवनसँग सम्बन्धित पूर्वाधार निर्माण गरिने सरकारको योजना छ।

अधिकार सम्पन्न बाग्मती सभ्यता एकीकृत विकास समितिले हटाइएका बस्ती रहेका स्थानमा स्थायी कङ्क्रिट संरचना निर्माण नगरी सबै नागरिकले सहज रूपमा उपयोग गर्न सक्ने खुला क्षेत्र विकास गरिने जनाएको छ।

समितिका आयोजना निर्देशक मचाकाजी महर्जनले नदीको प्राकृतिक बहाव संरक्षण, बाढी व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउने तथा सार्वजनिक प्रयोगका खुला क्षेत्र विकास गर्ने उद्देश्यले छुट्टै गुरुयोजना तयार भइरहेको जानकारी दिए।

उनका अनुसार उक्त गुरुयोजना अन्य विद्यमान सहरी योजनासँग तालमेल हुने गरी तयार पारिँदैछ। उनले भने, ‘हामी सबै नागरिकको पहुँच हुने खुला सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र निर्माण गर्दैछौँ। यहाँ पदमार्ग, हरित क्षेत्र र खुला मनोरञ्जनस्थल बन्नेछन्, तर स्थायी कङ्क्रिट भवन निर्माण गरिने छैन।’

महर्जनका अनुसार नदी व्यवस्थापनको उद्देश्य नदीलाई पर्खालभित्र सीमित गर्नु नभई प्राकृतिक बहावका लागि पर्याप्त खुला क्षेत्र सुरक्षित गर्नु हो।

अत्यधिक वर्षा वा बाढीका बेला नदी सहज रूपमा फैलिन सक्ने गरी खुला पार्क र हरित क्षेत्र विकास गरिने उनले बताए।

समितिका कार्यकारी समिति अध्यक्ष डा आनन्द सिंह भाटले बाग्मतीलाई बाढी नियन्त्रण, सरसफाइ र हरियालीसँग जोडिएको सार्वजनिक खुला क्षेत्रका रूपमा विकास गरिने बताए।

उनले भविष्यमा बाग्मती किनारमा हरियाली, खुला खेलमैदान र नागरिकमैत्री वातावरण देख्न पाइने विश्वास व्यक्त गरे।

बल्खु, बंशीघाट, थापाथली, गैरीगाउँ, सिनामङ्गल र शङ्खमूललगायत क्षेत्रमा हटाइएका बस्तीका अधिकांश भग्नावशेष (डेब्रिस) हटाउने काम लगभग सम्पन्न भइसकेको समितिले जनाएको छ। हटाइएका डेब्रिस र माटोलाई भू–आकृतिअनुसार व्यवस्थित रूपमा मिलाएर प्रयोग गरिएको छ।

महर्जनका अनुसार बंशीघाट क्षेत्रमा करिब एक मिटर जमिन पुरी घाँसे मैदान (ग्रासल्यान्ड) निर्माणका लागि तयारी गरिएको छ। त्यहाँ खेलकुदका लागि उपयुक्त खुला क्षेत्र विकास गर्नुका साथै वृक्षरोपण गरिनेछ।

आगामी दिनमा फुटबल मैदान, ब्याडमिन्टन कोर्टलगायत खेलकुद पूर्वाधार निर्माण गर्ने योजना रहेको उनले बताए।

विश्व निकेतन विद्यालय नजिक प्रशोधन केन्द्र (ट्रिटमेन्ट प्लान्ट) निर्माण गर्ने योजना रहेको र बंशीघाट क्षेत्रलाई विद्यालयले खेलकुद प्रयोजनका लागि प्रयोग गर्ने समझदारीसमेत भएको समितिले जनाएको छ।

बल्खु क्षेत्रमा नदीको बहाव क्षेत्र विस्तारलाई प्राथमिकता दिइने भएको छ। हाल करिब ४० मिटर चौडाइमा सीमित नदीलाई निर्धारित ८० मिटर बहाव क्षेत्रसम्म विस्तार गरी बाँकी भागमा हरित क्षेत्र, खुला पार्क तथा सार्वजनिक उपयोगका पूर्वाधार निर्माण गरिने योजना छ।

शङ्खमूल क्षेत्रमा खुला खेलमैदान तथा खेलकुद केन्द्र विकास गर्ने अवधारणा अघि सारिएको छ। गैरीगाउँ र सिनामंगल क्षेत्रमा हाल पाँचदेखि १० मिटर चौडाइमा रहेको नदीलाई न्यूनतम ३० मिटर चौडा बनाइनेछ।

त्यसपछि बाँकी क्षेत्रमा घाँसे मैदान, पार्किङ, प्रतीक्षास्थल, खुला पार्क तथा खेलकुदका संरचना निर्माण गरिने समितिले जनाएको छ।

थापाथली क्षेत्रमा नदीको बहाव क्षेत्र करिब ६० मिटर पुर्याइनेछ। त्यसपछि करिडोर सडकलाई थापाथली अस्पतालतर्फबाट पुलमुनि हुँदै बंशीघाटसम्म निरन्तर जोड्ने योजना रहेको छ। यस क्रममा सम्पदा र स्मारक क्षेत्रमा असर नपर्ने गरी डिजाइन तयार गरिने समितिले जनाएको छ।

समितिका अनुसार बल्खुमा रिटेनिङ वाल, नदी किनार व्यवस्थापन र पार्क निर्माणको काम अघि बढाइनेछ। सिनामङ्गल क्षेत्रमा करिडोर सडक, रिभर ट्रेनिङ वाल तथा नदी व्यवस्थापनका आयोजना समानान्तर रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गरिने तयारी छ।

समितिले गत आर्थिक वर्षमै गुरुयोजनाको प्रस्ताव तयार गरेको थियो। चालु आर्थिक वर्षका लागि नदी व्यवस्थापनका विभिन्न कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत करिब रु दुई अर्ब बजेट विनियोजन भएको छ।

सोही बजेटबाट विस्तृत डिजाइन र लागत अनुमान तयार भइरहेको छ। दशैँअघि ठेक्का सम्झौता सम्पन्न गरी निर्माण कार्य सुरु गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेको आयोजना निर्देशक महर्जनले बताए।

सहरी विकास मन्त्रालयसँगको सहकार्यमा बहुवर्षीय (एमटीएफ) ढाँचाअन्तर्गत आवश्यक बजेट सुनिश्चित गरी तीन वर्षभित्र योजना कार्यान्वयन गर्ने तयारी गरिएको समितिले जनाएको छ।

सरकारले चालु आर्थिक वर्षको बजेटमार्फत ‘भिजन काठमाडौं–२०४०’ कार्यान्वयन सुरु गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ। उक्त योजनाअन्तर्गत काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नदी करिडोरमा पूर्वाधार, पार्क निर्माण, एकीकृत फोहोरमैला व्यवस्थापन, ढलमुक्त नदी अभियान तथा नदी किनारमा हरियाली प्रवर्धनका कार्यक्रम अघि बढाइने उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अर्थमन्त्री वाग्लेलाई उद्योग मन्त्रीले भनिन्: बजेटका आठ सुधार कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयनमा लागेका छौँ
articles.summary:
चालु आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३/८४ को बजेट प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्ने उद्देश्यले अर्थ मन्त्रालयले सम्बन्धित मन्त्रालयसँग छलफललाई तीव्र बनाएको छ। यसैक्रममा उद्योग, वाणिज्य तथा आपूर्तिमन्त्री गौरीकुमारी यादवले उद्योग मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गत समेटिएका सुधारका कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयनका लागि मन्त्रालय सक्रिय रूपमा अघि बढिरहेको बताएकी छन्।

अर्थमन्त्री डा. स्वर्णिम वाग्लेको उपस्थितिमा बिहीबार आयोजित छलफलमा मन्त्री यादवले उद्योग मन्त्रालयको कार्यक्षेत्रभित्र पर्ने कानुनी तथा नीतिगत सुधारहरू निर्धारित कार्यतालिकाअनुसार अघि बढाइने जानकारी दिइन्।

उनले चालु बजेटमा उद्योग मन्त्रालयसँग सम्बन्धित आठ वटा प्रमुख सुधार कार्यक्रम समावेश रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै केही कार्यक्रमको कार्यान्वयन प्रक्रिया सुरु भइसकेको र बाँकी कार्यक्रम पनि चरणबद्ध रूपमा अघि बढाइने स्पष्ट पारिन्।

मन्त्री यादवले बजेटमा घोषणा गरिएका सुधारका योजना प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्न अर्थ मन्त्रालयसँग प्राविधिक सहयोग र आपसी समन्वय अपरिहार्य रहेको बताइन्। मन्त्रालयको जिम्मेवारीभित्रका काम समयमै सम्पन्न गर्न दुवै मन्त्रालयबीच निरन्तर सहकार्य हुने उनको भनाइ थियो।

छलफलका क्रममा अर्थमन्त्री डा. स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले उद्योग मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गत रहेका कानुनी तथा नीतिगत सुधारका कार्यलाई तीव्रता दिन आग्रह गर्दै आवश्यक विज्ञ, स्रोत–साधन तथा प्राविधिक सहयोग उपलब्ध गराउन अर्थ मन्त्रालय पूर्ण रूपमा तयार रहेको बताए।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको बजेटमा उद्योग, वाणिज्य तथा आपूर्ति मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गत कम्पनी ऐन संशोधन, दामासाहीसम्बन्धी ऐन परिमार्जन, उधारो असुली ऐन निर्माण, बौद्धिक सम्पत्ति संरक्षणसम्बन्धी नयाँ कानुन लगायत आठ वटा महत्वपूर्ण कानुनी तथा नीतिगत सुधारका कार्यक्रम समावेश छन्।

अर्थ मन्त्रालयले बजेट कार्यान्वयनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउन नियमित अनुगमन तथा सम्बन्धित मन्त्रालयहरूसँग प्रगति समीक्षा गर्ने कार्यतालिका समेत तयार गरी कार्यान्वयनमा ल्याएको जनाएको छ।

articles.title: शैक्षिक परामर्श व्यवसायमाथि धरौटीको व्यवस्था कायमै रहन्छ : शिक्षामन्त्री पोखरेल
articles.summary:
शिक्षा तथा खेलकुदमन्त्री सस्मित पोखरेलले शैक्षिक परामर्श व्यवसायीका लागि निर्धारण गरिएको रु २५ लाख धरौटीको व्यवस्थाबाट सरकार पछि नहट्ने बताएका छन्।

शिक्षासम्बन्धी विषयमा कलम चलाउने पत्रकारसँग शुक्रबार सिंहरदरबारस्थित मन्त्रालयमा छलफलका क्रममा मन्त्री पोखरेलले कतिपय व्यवासायीकै सुझावका आधारमा ‘शैक्षिक परामर्श, भाषा शिक्षण तथा तयारी कक्षा सञ्चालन तथा व्यवस्थापन नियमावली २०८३’ मार्फत गरिएको त्यस्तो व्यवस्था फिर्ता नहुने स्पष्ट पारेका हुन्।

तीन प्रतिशत समता शिक्षा शुल्कमा सरकार पछि हटे जस्तै परामर्श व्यवसायका सम्बन्धमा पनि सरकार पछि हट्ने त होइन भन्ने पत्रकारको प्रश्नमा मन्त्री पोखरेलले त्यस्तो सोच नभएको बताए।

मन्त्री पोखरेलले विद्यालय शिक्षा ऐनजस्ता कानुन निर्माण गर्दा भने सरोकार भएका पक्षसँग पूर्वपरामर्श गरिने पनि उल्लेख गरे।

उनले विश्विद्यायहरुलाई स्वायत्त र दलीय प्रभावमुक्त बनाउन नवनियुक्त उपकुलपतिहरूलाई आफ्नो सोचपत्रसहित अघि बढ्न आग्रह गरिएको जनाए।

नेपाल सरकारका प्रवक्ता पोखरेलले शैक्षिक संस्था र सरकारी कार्यालयमा सातामा दुई दिनका लागि दिइएको बिदाको पूर्ण उपयोग गर्न आग्रह गर्दै उक्त निर्णय पनि कुनै पुनः विचार नहुने बताए।

मन्त्री पोखरेलले चिकित्सक डा गोविन्द केसीले चलाएका अभियानप्रति आफू विगतदेखि नै पक्षधर रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनीसँग अनौपचारिक संवाद भइरहेको बताए।

articles.title: सरकारले आवश्यकताअनुसार उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणलाई निरन्तरता दिन्छ : परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालय
articles.summary:
सरकारले सबै मित्रराष्ट्रहरूसँगको सम्बन्धलाई प्रगाढ तुल्याउँदै आवश्यकताअनुसार उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणलाई पनि निरन्तरता दिने जनाएको छ।

परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयमा शुक्रबार आयोजित नियमित पत्रकार सम्मेलनमा सहसचिव एवं प्रवक्ता लोकबहादुर पौडेल क्षेत्रीले प्रचलित कूटनीतिक अभ्यास बमोजिम सरकारले उच्चस्तरीय भ्रमणको तयारी गरिरहेको जानकारी दिए।

राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी(रास्वपा)का अनुरोधका आधारमा सभापति रवि लामिछानेको चीन भ्रमणको सहजीकरण गर्न परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालय तयार रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै प्रवक्ता क्षेत्रीले कूटनीतिक आधारमा सबै भ्रमणहरू सम्पन्न हुने बताए।

‘राजनीतिक दलहरूबीच हुने भ्रमण वा आदानप्रदान सम्बन्धित दलहरूको विषय हो। त्यस्तो भ्रमणका लागि परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयको समन्वय वा कूटनीतिक सहजीकरण आवश्यक पर्ने अवस्था आएमा सम्बन्धित राजनीतिक दलको अनुरोधका आधारमा मन्त्रालयले आवश्यक सहजीकरण गर्नेछ’, उनले भने।

एक प्रश्नको जवाफमा उनले प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहका प्रमुख सल्लाहकार कुमार वेनको भारत भ्रमणबारे मन्त्रालय अनभिज्ञ रहेको बताए।

उनले सांस्कृतिक कूटनीति हरेक देशको कूटनीतिक अभ्यासको महत्त्वपूर्ण पक्ष भएको उल्लेख गर्दै यसलाई अझ प्रभावकारी र सुदृढ बनाउने नीति सरकारले लिएको जानकारी समेत दिए।

articles.title: Three Supreme Court justices pressured to resign or face impeachment, rights groups claim
articles.summary:
International rights organisations have expressed concern over what they describe as growing political interference in Nepal’s judiciary, warning that recent government actions could undermine the independence of the courts and weaken the rule of law.

In a joint statement, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, and the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) stated that changes made to the Constitutional Council Act through an executive ordinance, along with reported pressure on senior Supreme Court justices, posed a serious threat to judicial independence.

The groups said the government’s decision in May to amend the Constitutional Council Act through an ordinance, rather than through parliamentary legislation, violated constitutional principles and raised concerns about the process for appointing officials to key constitutional bodies, including the chief justice.

The amendment changed the quorum and voting requirements of the Constitutional Council, the body responsible for recommending appointments to major constitutional positions. The rights organisations said the changes increased the possibility of political influence over judicial appointments because government representatives already hold a majority of seats on the council.

“The independence of the judiciary is a cornerstone of the rule of law and an essential safeguard for the protection of human rights,” Ian Seiderman, senior legal and policy director at the ICJ said in the statement. “Any reform of Nepal’s justice system should strengthen, not weaken, the independence, impartiality and integrity of the courts.”

The groups also questioned the appointment of Manoj Kumar Sharma as chief justice, saying it departed from Nepal’s long-standing practice of appointing the senior-most serving justice.

Although three senior judges remain on the Supreme Court, Sharma was appointed chief justice after being endorsed by the Parliamentary Hearing Committee. The organisations said complaints raised against his nomination were not subjected to meaningful public scrutiny.

The groups claimed that they had received credible reports that three senior Supreme Court justices, Sapana Pradhan Malla, Kumar Regmi and Hari Phuyal, had been pressured to resign under the threat of impeachment.

They said they were not aware of any publicly stated allegations against the judges that would meet the constitutional requirements for impeachment.

Under Nepal’s constitution, the initiation of impeachment proceedings automatically suspends a judge until Parliament determines whether the charges are valid. The organisations warned that suspending three senior Supreme Court justices could significantly affect the court’s functioning at a time when it is hearing important constitutional cases challenging government decisions and executive actions.

“Using or threatening to use impeachment against judges without clear constitutional justification risks creating the perception that constitutional procedures are being used to influence the composition of the court and potentially the outcome of pending cases,” the groups said.

They noted that Nepal has previously faced criticism over attempts to use impeachment proceedings against judges in ways that could compromise judicial independence.

“Public confidence in the judiciary depends not only on the competence and integrity of judges but also on the transparency, fairness and independence of judicial appointments,” said Meenakshi Ganguly, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Appointments or removals that appear susceptible to political influence undermine confidence in the administration of justice and weaken the rule of law.”

International standards require judges to be protected from improper influence, pressure, threats and interference. The removal of judges must be based on objective criteria and safeguarded against political manipulation, the organisations said.

The groups acknowledged that judicial reform may be necessary in Nepal but said any reform process should strengthen institutional independence, transparency and accountability rather than increase political control over the judiciary.

“The objective of judicial reform should be to build stronger, more independent institutions that enjoy public confidence, not institutions that are more vulnerable to political pressure,” said Isabelle Lassee, acting regional director for South Asia at Amnesty International.

The organisations urged the Nepal government to stop “exerting pressure on judges to resign and avoid impeachment proceedings” unless there are clearly established constitutional grounds and due process safeguards.

They also called on authorities to ensure that judicial appointments, including the appointment of the chief justice, are conducted through transparent, objective and merit-based procedures.

The groups further urged Parliament to review amendments to the Constitutional Council Act through an open legislative process and ensure that future judicial reforms comply with Nepal’s constitution, the principles of separation of powers, and international standards on judicial independence.

articles.title: Built for adventure, held back by regulations
articles.summary:
Namche Bazar, the gateway to Mount Everest, sits along the trail to the world's highest peak. Perched at 3,400 metres above sea level, the bustling Sherpa town overlooks the Dudh Koshi river. Suspended above the river on the old Hillary Bridge once stood Everest Bungee run by Chhepal Dorji Sherpa.

In 2024, after securing the required approvals from Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality and Sagarmatha National Park, Sherpa imported specialised equipment from India and France and launched the bungee operation. By then, he had already invested Rs14 million in the project.

Exactly a year after obtaining the permits, the attraction opened to visitors in 2025. Sherpa envisioned giving trekkers and mountaineers heading for Everest a brief but unforgettable thrill: a 145-foot plunge above the roaring Dudh Koshi river.

The business quickly began attracting customers. Visitor numbers were growing, and the future looked promising.

The optimism did not last long.

Someone filed a complaint with the District Administration Office in Salleri, questioning how a private company had been allowed to operate a commercial business from a government-owned bridge over a public river.

Following the complaint, the bungee operation was shut down.

"What exactly was my mistake?" Sherpa said in an interview with Kantipur. "I started the business only after receiving approval from the local government and the national park. Later, however, I was shown different provisions of different laws."

The complaint marked the beginning of a long bureaucratic ordeal.

Sherpa found himself shuttling between the Department of Tourism in Kathmandu, government offices in Lukla and Namche, and a maze of different authorities. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, the local government, the Department of Tourism, the Cottage and Small Industries Office and the Office of the Company Registrar all had separate procedures, requirements and jurisdictions.

Unable to navigate the overlapping bureaucracy, Sherpa eventually gave up.

"Every government office has its own process," he said. "After exhausting every option, I spent nearly Rs4 million dismantling and removing all the bungee infrastructure."

He is now building a new "single-pillar bungee" on nearby private land. Around Rs50 million has already been invested in the new project.

"I expect to begin operations from the new site within the next three months," said Sherpa, who is currently in Kathmandu. "All the necessary procedures are now in their final stage."

Sherpa's experience is far from unique.

For many investors entering Nepal's growing adventure tourism industry, navigating the legal system has become almost as challenging as building the attractions themselves. Across the sector, entrepreneurs tell remarkably similar stories of regulatory confusion, overlapping jurisdictions and prolonged administrative delays.

The result is not simply procedural frustration. Investors say vague and inconsistent government policies are preventing large investments from generating the returns they were designed to produce.

A similar story is unfolding in the foothills of Shivapuri hill, north of Kathmandu.

Ram Avatar Yadav, operations head of Shivapuri Thrill Adventure Park, has spent years dealing with bureaucratic hurdles much like those faced by Sherpa.

Spread across 24 ropani of land (one ropani equals 0.05087 hectares), the park is already operating, but its licensing process remains incomplete.

Recalling the administrative difficulties involved in building the nearly Rs110 million project, Yadav said entrepreneurs are often forced to submit the same documents repeatedly to multiple agencies.

"We had already obtained approval from Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park to build and operate the park," Yadav said. "Only afterwards did we find out that the law also required a separate operating licence from the Department of Tourism."

The park has already completed its environmental assessment. Yadav has submitted all the required documents listed in the Department of Tourism's licensing checklist and is now waiting for the next step.

"Once the documents are reviewed, officials will conduct a field inspection," a department official said. "If everything meets the prescribed requirements, the operating licence will be issued."

The park currently offers ten different adventure activities and employs 20 people.

Charging between Rs200 and Rs700 per head, it attracts around 300 Nepali and foreign visitors a day.

Bungee and adventure parks are only part of Nepal's expanding adventure tourism industry.

Across the country, businesses now operate ziplining, canyoning, heli-diving, skiing, heli-skiing and at least 17 other adventure tourism activities.

Yet entrepreneurs behind these ventures say they face an entirely different kind of challenge, one that has little to do with tourism and everything to do with bureaucracy.

Licensing, permits, regulation and renewals all remain under the Department of Tourism, a federal government agency. At the same time, businesses are also required to complete separate approval processes with local and provincial governments.

Since Nepal adopted federalism, authority to register and regulate hotels, homestays, travel agencies and trekking companies has largely been devolved to provincial and local governments.

Adventure tourism, however, remains an exception.

Under Nepal's tourism laws, only the Department of Tourism has the authority to license adventure sports operations. Although these businesses form part of the broader tourism sector, responsibility for regulating them has remained firmly with the federal government.

The department itself lacks even basic industry-wide data.

It does not maintain consolidated figures showing how many small and large adventure tourism companies are operating across Nepal, how much they have invested or how many jobs they have created.

According to director general Ramkrishna Lamichhane, the department began tightening oversight after receiving complaints that some businesses were operating adventure activities without obtaining official licences.

Lamichhane said only 56 companies nationwide are officially licensed to operate adventure tourism businesses.

After complaints emerged that several operators were bypassing government procedures, the Department of Tourism issued a public notice on May 4 requiring all operators of unregistered adventure activities, including bungee jumping, canyoning, rock climbing, ziplining, speedboats, skywalks, ultra-trails and fun parks, to register their businesses and obtain licences by mid-June.

That deadline has now expired.

According to the department, however, the response fell well short of expectations.

"Even after giving operators more than one month to register, most of them did not enter the department's licensing process," one department official said. "Only five or six businesses came forward to begin the approval process. It appears many more are still operating without licences."

The Department of Tourism has made environmental assessments a mandatory part of the licensing process, with the level of assessment determined by the size of the investment.

Projects with investments exceeding Rs20 million are required to complete a Brief Environmental Study, while those involving infrastructure worth more than Rs50 million must undergo an Initial Environmental Examination.

The irony, however, is that environmental approvals do not fall under the Department of Tourism's jurisdiction. They are handled by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, adding another layer to an already cumbersome approval process. Environmental assessments cannot be completed within days. They often take months, delaying projects long before tourism authorities can begin processing operating licences.

The Tourism Act, 1978 classifies adventure activities under the broad category of "other tourism businesses". But entrepreneurs and officials alike say the definition has failed to keep pace with the industry's rapid evolution.

Modern attractions such as motorboats, skywalks, sky cycling and amusement parks are not specifically covered by the law.

To address the gap, the Department of Tourism had begun drafting separate regulations that would formally recognise and regulate these emerging activities. The effort, however, stalled after the new Tourism Bill was approved by the National Assembly but became stuck in the House of Representatives.

As new technologies and adventure sports continue to emerge, Nepal's legal framework has struggled to keep up, leaving regulators uncertain about how many of these businesses should be governed.

The consequences are already evident.

One example lies along the Babai river in Dang district.

In April 2024, Hanshraj KC, together with Dipak KC, Umesh Dangi and Jeet Bahadur Dangi, invested Rs6 million to launch two motorboats on the Babai river at Motipur. The partners hoped to build a business that would allow them to remain in their village while earning a livelihood through agriculture and tourism.

They constructed a small reservoir by building a weir near a suspension bridge used by residents to cross the river and began operating the boats.

Then the pattern that had played out in Sherpa's case repeated itself.

The entrepreneurs initially tried to register their business with the Department of Tourism. Following advice from the department, they instead submitted an application to the Nepal Shipping Office in Ekantakuna and began operating.

Soon afterwards, someone lodged a complaint with the District Administration Office.

Acting on the complaint, the chief district officer ordered the operation to shut down.

"We operated for only 15 days," said KC. "Around 10,000 people had already used the service, but after the complaint we were forced to close immediately."

According to Rajan Pradhan, acting registrar at the Nepal Shipping Office, a new Shipping Bill drafted by the office proposes making official approval mandatory for all motorised water transport services.

Although the previous government succeeded in passing the bill through the National Assembly, it has remained pending in the House of Representatives following a change in government.

Without a clear legal framework, Pradhan said, the office has been unable to process applications such as the one submitted by KC.

Most adventure tourism businesses in Nepal are not located in cities. They are typically built in forests, along rivers, beside lakes, or on remote hillsides far from urban centres.

To operate such businesses, private investors often need to lease government land or public assets, including rivers, forests, lakes, ponds and bridges, for a fixed period.

Those leases must be processed through the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration.

However, officials at the Department of Tourism say another layer of uncertainty emerged after the government scrapped the Working Policy on Registration, Usage and Leasing of Government Land, 2022 in mid-june 2026.

The decision has created fresh uncertainty for adventure tourism businesses operating on public land, those awaiting approval and those still in the planning stage.

"Whether it is a river, a stream or a waterfall, any adventure activity that involves investment on public property requires approval from the federal government," said Himal Gautam, director at the Department of Tourism.

"Even relatively small investments connected to public property must ultimately be approved by the federal Cabinet under the current legal framework."

Gautam acknowledged that while many entrepreneurs approach the department seeking licences, the department itself often lacks the legal tools needed to process their applications.

"Even when people come to us intending to comply with the law, we cannot always provide them with a legal pathway," he said. "Multiple laws administered by multiple agencies apply simultaneously, while many of the required regulations have yet to be drafted."

Faced with unclear policies on the one hand and an exhausting bureaucratic process on the other, many entrepreneurs now hand over the entire licensing process to legal and consultancy firms after spending months navigating government offices themselves.

These firms prepare environmental assessments, coordinate with government agencies and obtain the various approvals required under the country's regulatory system.

Yadav, operations head of Shivapuri Thrill Adventure Park, said overlapping jurisdictions and conflicting rules across government agencies have become one of the biggest obstacles facing investors.

"Many different laws apply to a single project," he said. "The same work has to be repeated over and over. It becomes much easier to hand everything over to professional consultants."

The experiences of Sherpa in Solukhumbu, KC in Dang and Yadav in Kathmandu were echoed by other entrepreneurs and stakeholders interviewed by Kantipur.

Some described becoming trapped in overlapping federal, provincial and local procedures. Others said they learned about key legal requirements only after making substantial investments.

The confusion is affecting not only private investors but also local governments.

Manebhanjyang Rural Municipality in Okhaldhunga offers another example.

For the past two years, the local government has been operating a zipline at Kettuke in Manebhanjyang without obtaining approval from the Department of Tourism.

Rural Municipality Chair Gyanendra Rumdali said the municipality built the attraction with a budget of Rs5 million after consulting local elected representatives as part of efforts to promote tourism.

"We had no idea at the beginning that we also needed approval from the Department of Tourism under the federal government," Rumdali said. "Only later did we realise that several legal requirements had not been fulfilled."

After the Department of Tourism issued its public notice requiring operators to obtain licences, the municipality began the legal process to secure official approval.

Rumdali added that because helicopters also fly through the area where the zipline is located, the municipality has formally informed the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal about the installation to minimise the risk of accidents caused by the zipline cables.

Along the Janakpur-Dhalkebar road at Ramdaiya stands Wonderland Water Park, one of Madhesh province's newest leisure destinations.

With water slides, artificial wave pools and fountains, the park has become a popular attraction not only for residents but also for visitors from across the nearby Indian border.

Spread over 300,000 square feet, the park was built with an investment of Rs120 million and has been operating since 2025.

For its owner, Janakpur entrepreneur Guddu Jain, however, running an adventure and recreational tourism business has proved far more challenging than building one.

"In India, my friends are operating similar facilities after obtaining approval from a single government office," Jain said. "Here, you have to run from one office to another, from the local unit all the way to the federal government, for registration, licence renewals and other approvals. The procedures involving both local and federal authorities are unnecessarily complicated."

According to Jain, the problem lies less with the regulations themselves than with the fragmented way government agencies implement them.

Operating a water park requires trained lifeguards capable of rescuing visitors at risk of drowning. Nepal, however, has only a limited pool of qualified personnel, forcing him to recruit lifeguards from India.

That is where another bureaucratic obstacle emerges.

"All employees, including lifeguards, must be paid through bank transfers," Jain said. "But foreign workers cannot easily open bank accounts in Nepal. First, you have to travel to Kathmandu and obtain approval from the Labour Office. Even that is not enough. They now also have to be enrolled in the Social Security Fund."

Most of the Indian workers he hires come to Nepal for only six months.

"They simply don't want to get caught up in all these government procedures," Jain said. "They want to receive their wages easily. They have no interest in spending their time running from one government office to another."

Jain said the communication gap between different levels of government became evident when the Department of Tourism issued a public notice in May requiring unregistered adventure tourism businesses to obtain licences.

"The provincial tourism office in Janakpur wasn't even aware of the notice," he said.

"I learned about it through a news report and went to the Madhesh tourism office to ask about it. They had no information whatsoever."

For Jain, the episode exposed a deeper problem: weak coordination between federal, provincial and local governments in regulating Nepal's adventure and recreational tourism industry.

According to Gautam, information officer at the Department of Tourism, federalism has changed the way tourism businesses are established, but not the way adventure tourism is regulated.

Since the introduction of the federal system, many tourism businesses have been registered through local governments. However, the authority to license and regulate adventure activities remains exclusively with the federal government.

The problem, Gautam said, is that the legal framework has failed to keep pace with the industry's rapid expansion.

"Today, almost every hotel and resort wants to offer some form of adventure activity to enhance the visitor experience, and new facilities continue to be built," he said. "But the existing laws were not designed to regulate all of these emerging activities."

"What Nepal needs now is legislation that reflects the realities of today's adventure tourism industry. Once the legal framework is in place, we can register businesses, regulate them and renew their licences accordingly. But without clear laws, how are we supposed to do that?"

articles.title: जानकी मन्दिरको गद्दीमा रस्साकस्सी : महन्त अडिग, उत्तराधिकारी सक्रिय
articles.summary:
जनकपुरधामस्थित जानकी मन्दिरमा नयाँ महन्त नियुक्तिका लागि गुठी संस्थानले प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाएको छ। महन्त रामतपेश्वर दास वैष्णवको पाँच वर्षे नियुक्ति अवधि सकिएपछि संस्थानले पुनः महन्त नियुक्त गर्ने तयारी थालेको हो।

महन्त दासको नियुक्ति अवधि समाप्त भएको लामो समय बितिसक्दा पनि उनले कार्यभार नछाडेपछि गुठी सञ्चालन ऐनअनुसार नयाँ महन्त नियुक्तिको प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको हो। करिब २० वर्षदेखि उनी जानकी मन्दिरका महन्तका रूपमा रहेका छन्। तर यसपटक उनलाई विस्थापित गर्दै उत्तराधिकारी महन्त रामरोशन दास मुख्य महन्त बन्ने दौडमा सक्रिय देखिएका छन्।

रामरोशन दासमाथि फर्जी उत्तराधिकारी परिचयपत्र बनाएको आरोप लागेपछि विवाद अदालत पुगेको थियो। केही महिनाअघि अदालतले उत्तराधिकारसम्बन्धी विवादमा फैसला गरेको थियो।

अदालतको फैसला रामरोशनको पक्षमा आएपछि गुठी संस्थानले उनलाई अनुकूल हुने गरी नयाँ मुख्य महन्त नियुक्तिको प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएको हो।

महन्त रामतपेश्वरको नियुक्ति अवधि सकिएको वर्षौं बितिसक्दा पनि संस्थानले त्यसतर्फ खास चासो दिएको थिएन। तर रामरोशनको उत्तराधिकारसम्बन्धी विवाद समाधान भएको केही महिनामै नयाँ महन्त नियुक्तिको प्रक्रिया सुरु भएपछि उनकै पहलमा संस्थान सक्रिय भएको संकेत मिलेको छ।

यसपटक रामरोशन महन्त रामतपेश्वरलाई हटाएर स्वयं मुख्य महन्त बन्ने प्रयासमा छन्। जसरी पनि नियुक्तिपत्र प्राप्त गर्ने उद्देश्यसहित उनी प्रतिस्पर्धामा उत्रिएका छन्। उनीनिकट स्रोतका अनुसार उत्तराधिकार विवाद पहिल्यै समाधान भएको भए उनी यसअघि नै महन्त बनिसक्ने थिए। केही महिनाअघि मात्रै उक्त विवाद टुंगिएपछि उनी अहिले मुख्य लक्ष्यतर्फ केन्द्रित भएका छन्।

महन्त रामतपेश्वरले आफू बिरामी भई उपचारका लागि बाहिर रहेका बेला किर्ते हस्ताक्षर गरी आफूलाई जानकी मन्दिरको उत्तराधिकारी महन्त घोषणा गरिएको आरोप लगाएपछि विवाद अदालत पुगेको थियो। तर उनीमाथि लगाइएका आरोप पुष्टि नभएपछि अदालतले रामरोशनको पक्षमा फैसला सुनाएको थियो।

अदालतको फैसलापछि उत्साहित रामरोशन यसपटक मुख्य महन्त बन्ने तयारीमा छन्। आवश्यक समन्वय र पहलमार्फत महन्त रामतपेश्वरलाई हटाएर गद्दीमा पुग्ने रणनीतिमा रहेको स्रोतको दाबी छ।

स्रोतका अनुसार रामरोशनले गुठी संस्थान शाखा कार्यालय, जनकपुरका प्रमुख किशोरकुमार झासँग प्रारम्भिक छलफल गरिसकेका छन्।

जनकपुर शाखाबाट सकारात्मक संकेत पाएपछि उनी गुठी संस्थानको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय काठमाडौंमा समेत सक्रिय भएका छन्। गुरु–शिष्य परम्पराभन्दा गुठी संस्थान ऐनअनुसार महन्त नियुक्त गर्न सर्वोच्च अदालतले निर्देशन दिएपछि उनी संस्थानमा सक्रिय रूपमा दौडधुप गरिरहेका छन्।

स्रोतका अनुसार गुठी संस्थान, जनकपुर शाखाका प्रमुखले पनि रामरोशनलाई महन्त बनाउन चाहेको चर्चा छ। तर शाखा प्रमुख किशोरकुमार झाले आफूले कुनै व्यक्तिको नाम सिफारिस नगरेको बताएका छन्।

उनले भने, “२०७० माघ १७ गते गुठी संस्थानले रामतपेश्वर दासलाई हटाएर जगदीश दास वैष्णवलाई महन्त नियुक्त गरेको थियो। त्यसविरुद्ध रामतपेश्वर सर्वोच्च अदालत जानुभएको थियो। सर्वोच्चले उहाँकै पक्षमा फैसला गरेपछि हालसम्म उहाँ नै महन्त हुनुहुन्छ।”

झाले थप भने, “२०८०–८१ मा सर्वोच्च अदालतले पुजारीलगायत जनशक्ति व्यवस्थापन निर्देशिकाअनुसार महन्त नियुक्त गर्न आदेश दिएपछि सोहीअनुसार प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको हो। रामतपेश्वर दास पुनः महन्त बन्न निवेदन दिनुहुन्छ वा रामरोशन आउनुहुन्छ, त्यो उहाँहरूको विषय हो। हामी गुठी ऐनअनुसार प्रक्रिया मात्रै अघि बढाइरहेका छौं।”

गुठी संस्थानले महन्त नियुक्तिको प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएपछि आफू पनि इच्छुक रहेको उत्तराधिकारी महन्त रामरोशनले बताएका छन्।

उनले भने, “अहिलेका महन्तको उमेर ७५ वर्ष नाघिसकेको छ। उहाँ आफैं हिँड्न सक्नुहुन्न, उठाउन–बसाल्न दुई जना मानिस चाहिन्छ। तपाईंहरू पनि सहयोग गर्नुस्, हामीलाई अवसर दिनुस्, जानकी मन्दिर राम्रोसँग चलाएर देखाउँछु।”

उनले थप भने, “बुढो महन्तबारे पनि समाचार लेख्नुस्। उहाँ जबर्जस्ती लामो समयदेखि महन्त भएर बस्नुभएको छ। सरकारले जानकी मन्दिरमा हस्तक्षेप गरे सरकार तीन टुक्रा हुन्छ भनेर उहाँले बोलेको अडियो पनि सार्वजनिक गर्नुस्।”

जानकी मन्दिरनिकट स्रोतका अनुसार रामरोशन अहिले मुख्य महन्त बन्ने अभियानमा छन्। त्यसका लागि उनले पहिले महन्त रामतपेश्वरलाई विश्वासमा लिने, नभए अन्य विकल्प अपनाएर पनि यसपटक मुख्य महन्त बन्ने प्रयास गरिरहेका छन्।

स्रोतका अनुसार महन्त रामतपेश्वर सहमत नभएपछि गुठी संस्थानको केन्द्रीय कार्यालयका पदाधिकारीलाई आर्थिक प्रभावमा पारेर नियुक्ति लिने प्रयाससमेत भइरहेको चर्चा छ। मन्दिरमा आयोजना हुने विभिन्न कार्यक्रममा पनि रामरोशनको सक्रियता मुख्य महन्तभन्दा बढी देखिन थालेको बताइन्छ।

रामरोशनको प्रभाव बढ्दै गएपछि महन्त रामतपेश्वरले आफूले कसैलाई उत्तराधिकारी महन्त नियुक्त नगरेको र रामरोशनले किर्ते हस्ताक्षर गरी आफूलाई उत्तराधिकारी घोषणा गरेको दाबी सार्वजनिक रूपमा गर्दै आएका थिए। त्यसपछि विवाद अदालत पुगेको थियो। अदालतले हस्ताक्षर किर्ते नभएको ठहर गरेपछि उत्तराधिकारसम्बन्धी विवाद साम्य भएको हो।

महन्त रामतपेश्वर दास र उत्तराधिकारी महन्त रामरोशन दास नाताले मामा–भान्जा हुन्। उनीहरूबीच शक्ति र स्रोतको विषयलाई लिएर लामो समयदेखि आन्तरिक विवाद रहँदै आएको छ। विशेषगरी जानकी मन्दिरमा कुनै ठूलो कार्यक्रम हुँदा उक्त विवाद सार्वजनिक हुने गरेको छ।

सप्ताहव्यापी रूपमा मनाइने विवाहपञ्चमी महोत्सवका बेला उनीहरूबीचको विवाद सञ्चारमाध्यममार्फत बाहिर आएको थियो। त्यसबेला महन्त रामतपेश्वरले मन्दिरको जिम्मेवारी दिएका रामरोशनमाथि अपारदर्शितासहित विभिन्न आरोप लगाएका थिए। त्यसपछि मन्दिरभित्रको विवाद सार्वजनिक भएको थियो।

महन्त दासले रामरोशनलाई ‘स्वघोषित उत्तराधिकारी महन्त’ भन्दै सञ्चारमाध्यममा अभिव्यक्ति दिएपछि विवाद थप चर्किएको थियो। तर केही दिनपछि उनले आवेगमा आएर त्यस्तो अभिव्यक्ति दिएको स्वीकार गरेका थिए।

यसअघि गुठी संस्थानले रामतपेश्वर दासले गुठीको जग्गा अतिक्रमण गरेको र नियुक्तिको सर्तअनुसार आय–व्यय विवरण नबुझाएको आरोप लगाउँदै उनलाई हटाएर जगदीश दास वैष्णवलाई महन्त नियुक्त गरेको थियो।

जगदीश दास वैष्णवलाई महन्त नियुक्त गरिएपछि जानकी मन्दिरमा महन्त गुरु–शिष्य परम्पराबाट नियुक्त हुनुपर्ने माग गर्दै रामतपेश्वर पक्षधर आन्दोलनमा उत्रिएका थिए। आन्दोलनका क्रममा गुठी संस्थान, जनकपुर शाखामा तालाबन्दीसमेत गरिएको थियो।

त्यसै क्रममा तत्कालीन गुठी प्रमुख दीपक पाण्डेलाई कालोमोसो दलेको अभियोगमा जिल्ला अदालतले रामतपेश्वर दासलाई दोषी ठहर गर्दै पाँच हजार रुपैयाँ जरिवानाको फैसला सुनाएको थियो।

articles.title: काठमाडौं प्रहरीका ६१ प्रतिशत मुद्दाको ‘डिजिटल अभिलेख’
articles.summary:
जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर काठमाडौंले परिसर र मातहत दर्ता भएकामध्ये ६१ प्रतिशत बढी मुद्दाको ‘डिजिटल अभिलेख’ तयार गरेको छ।

गत असार मसान्तसम्म दर्ता भएका कुल ११ हजार ७८ मध्ये छ हजार ८६१ मुद्दाका फाइल स्क्यान गरिएको परिसरका प्रवक्ता एवं प्रहरी उपरीक्षक पवनकुमार भट्टराईले जानकारी दिए।

परिसरका दुई हजार ८७, महाराजगञ्ज वृत्तका ३८८, बौद्धका ७१४, गौशालाका ३९०, बानेश्वरका ३६६, कालिमाटीका ५७५, कीर्तिपुरका ९०, थानकोटका ३९७, स्वयम्भूका ४१०, बालाजुका ४५७, लैनचौरका ३३४, दरबारमार्गका १३५, जनसेवाका २४६, सिंहदरबारका १२९ र वृत्त मालिगाउँका १४३ मुद्दा स्क्यान गरिएका छन्।

परिसरमा शुक्रबार आयोजित पत्रकार सम्मेलनमा प्रहरी उपरीक्षक भट्टराईले तस्करी, लागुऔषध ओसारपसार, ठगी, चोरी, जबरजस्ती करणीलगायत आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि भएका एक हजार ८७१ जनाको ‘प्रोफाइल’ तयार पारिएको बताए।

परिसरबाट प्रदान हुँदै आएका सेवालाई प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउँदै लगिएको जानकारी दिँदै उनले पुस महिनादेखि असारसम्म अनलाइनबाट दुई हजार २७६ मुद्दाको म्याद थप गरिएको बताए। गत आवमा ११ हजार ७८ मुद्दा दर्ता भएकामा आठ हजार ५८१ अभियुक्तलाई पक्राउ गरिएको छ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ मा घटेका मुख्य अपराधको सङ्ख्या ८५ प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी रहेको छ। परिसरका अनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी बैंकिङ कसुरका चार हजार ४७९, अभद्र व्यवहारका एक हजार ७०२, चोरीका एक हजार ८९, लागुऔषधका ६७०, ठगीका ६३८, अपराधिक उपद्रवका १७५, आत्महत्याका ३४९, जबरजस्तीकरणीका २६९, ज्यानमार्ने उद्योगका १२२ र सवारी ज्यानका ९९ वटा घटना भएका थिए।

लागुऔषधसम्बन्धी कसुरमा मुद्दा दर्ता बढ्यो

पछिल्लो तीन वर्षमा लागुऔषध कसुरसम्बन्धी मुद्दा दर्ता गर्ने क्रम बढेको छ। गत आवमा सोसम्बन्धी ६७० मुद्दा दर्ता भएका थिए।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१/८२ मा ४३१ र आव २०८०/८१ मा ३३३ वटा मुद्दा दर्ता भएका परिसरका प्रवक्ता भट्टराईले जानकारी दिए।

गत आवमा फैसला कार्यान्वयन गर्ने क्रममा दुई हजार ४०७ जना पक्राउ परेका थिए। सोबापत रु २२ करोड ६४ लाख ८६ हजार २४० जरिवाना र ५१९ वर्ष आठ महिना नौ दिन कैद असुल भएको छ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ मा क्यासिनो ठगी, नक्कली पैसा छपाइ, हुण्डी तथा अभौतिक मुद्रा कारोबारमा संलग्नलाई कारबाही गरिएको परिसरका प्रवक्ता भट्टराईले जानकारी दिए।

articles.title: आन्तरिक राजस्व कार्यालय विराटनगरबाट १० अर्ब राजस्व सङ्कलन
articles.summary:
आन्तरिक राजस्व कार्यालय विराटनगरले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ मा कूल रु १० अर्ब ३० करोड ५३ लाख ३६ हजार राजस्व सङ्कलन गरेको छ।

सो अवधिमा कार्यालयले रु १२ अर्ब १० करोड २८ लाख ८० हजार राजस्व सङ्कलन गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेकामा रु एक अर्ब ७९ करोड ७५ लाख ४४ हजार राजस्व कम उठेको कार्यालय प्रमुख केशवप्रसाद उप्रेतीले जानकारी दिए। कार्यालयले ८५ दशमलव १५ प्रतिशत प्रगति गरेको उनले बताए।

सङ्कलित राजस्वमा आयकर रु चार अर्ब सात करोड २५ लाख ४१ हजार, बहाल आयकर रु आठ करोड आठ लाख ५५ हजार, ब्याज कर रु ३८ करोड १३ लाख एक हजार, मूल्य अभिवृद्धि कर रु दुई अर्ब ५६ करोड ८६ लाख ७५ हजार, अन्तःशुल्क रु तीन अर्ब १५ करोड १० लाख ४९ हजार, शिक्षा कर रु ८४ हजार र अन्य कर रु पाँच करोड आठ लाख ३२ हजार रहेको छ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८०/८१ मा रु नौ अर्ब ४४ करोड राजस्व सङ्कलन गर्ने लक्ष्य लिएकामा रु आठ अर्ब ९३ करोड, आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१/८२ मा रु १० अर्ब ७२ करोड राजस्व सङ्कलन गर्ने लक्ष्य लिएकामा रु नौ अर्ब ६१ करोड राजस्व सङ्कलन गरेको प्रमुख उप्रेतीले बताए।

तुलनात्मक रुपमा आर्थिक वर्ष २०८०/८१ मा आठ दशमलव ७७ प्रतिशत, आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१/८२ मा सात दशमलव ६१ प्रतिशत र आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ मा सात दशमलव २८ प्रतिशत राजस्व वृद्धि भएको उनले बताए।

यस कार्यालयमा कूल ६० हजार ६७५ करदाता आबद्ध रहेका छन्।

articles.title: बर्दियामा लागु औषधसहित एकजना पक्राउ
articles.summary:
लागु औषधसहित एक जनालाई प्रहरीले पक्राउ गरेको छ । बढैयाताल गाउँपालिका–२ फुटाहा स्थितबाट लागु औषध ब्राउन सुगरसहित प्रहरीले शुक्रबार एक जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको हो ।

पक्राउ पर्नेमा जिल्ला झापा, झापा गाउँपालिका–६ का ३३ वर्षीय अभिषेक केसी रहेका छन् । भारतको बलई गाउँ बजारबाट शंकास्पद रुपमा नेपालतर्फ आईरहेको अवस्थामा केसीलाई नियन्त्रणमा लिई चेकजाँच गर्दा कालो प्लाष्टिकमा बेरेर मलद्वारमा लुकाई छिपाई राखेको अवस्थामा लागु औषध फेला परेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ ।
